notes_list.title: Carbanions — Stability and Geometry
notes_list.basic_overview: Carbanions contain a carbon bearing a negative charge and a lone pair. Their geometry and stability depend strongly on hybridization, substituents and resonance.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Electron-withdrawing groups and resonance stabilize carbanions; alkyl groups usually destabilize localized carbanions. Hybridization trend often favors sp > sp2 > sp3 for negative-charge stabilization at carbon.
notes_list.examples: Acetylide ions, enolates and benzylic carbanions are common stabilized examples.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: Strong bases generate carbanions/enolates; polar aprotic solvents often enhance nucleophilicity of anions.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: 1. Locate lone pair. 2. Determine resonance. 3. Check electron-withdrawing groups. 4. Assess hybridization. 5. Consider ion pairing/solvent.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Formation of a carbanion is governed by acid-base equilibrium; its reaction with electrophiles can be fast and often diffusion-controlled in suitable media.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Core for enolate chemistry, alkylation and organometallic reactions.
notes_list.common_traps: Do not rank carbanions by the same order as carbocations; electron donation and withdrawal have opposite effects.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
